slides.headline: A $10,000 BITCOIN INVOICE ARRIVED WORTH $7,200 THREE DAYS LATER, 6 AI PROMPTS WRITE THE CLAUSE THAT STOPS IT
slides.image_prompt: Dario Amodei in orange apron, manic grin, slams stack of prompt sheets onto night-market counter as gold Bitcoin coins spray. Claude logo blazes in copper neon. Documentary 35mm photo, harsh flash, amber-gold on electric teal.

slides.headline: MOST BUSINESS OWNERS LEARN THIS FROM AN IRS NOTICE
slides.body: Every crypto payment creates a legal event your current contracts, taxes, and payment policy were not built for. The six prompts below write what most businesses pay $1,500 to $3,000 per document to an attorney for, each one takes under four minutes to run.
slides.image_prompt: Two hands on a cluttered desk: one grips a tax form stamped with a large red warning triangle, the other holds a phone showing a crypto wallet's $ balance. A torn government envelope lies open beside a calculator. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh flash, grain. Accent: sharp gold on cool white.

slides.headline: 1) CALCULATE YOUR CRYPTO TAX BILL BEFORE THE IRS DOES
slides.body: Paste this into Claude: 'I received [amount] in [coin] on [date] at $[price per coin]. Calculate my taxable gain, the ordinary income tax owed at 37%, and the dollar amount I should set aside today.' Every crypto payment triggers a taxable event the moment it lands, most business owners find out in April, after the bill has already grown.

slides.headline: 2) WRITE A CRYPTO PAYMENT POLICY IN 4 MINUTES
slides.body: With your tax exposure calculated in step 1, lock in your acceptance rules. Paste this: 'Write a business crypto payment policy. We accept Bitcoin and Ethereum. The exchange rate locks at invoice creation. Overpayments convert to account credit. Include a volatility disclaimer.' A business attorney charges $1,500 to $3,000 for this document.

slides.headline: US BUSINESSES PAID $172 BILLION IN CARD FEES LAST YEAR
slides.body: Most crypto processors charge under 1%. The math is simple when the rules change.

slides.headline: 3) DRAFT THE CONTRACT CLAUSE THAT PROTECTS YOU
slides.body: Your policy covers which coins you accept, this clause locks the price on every individual deal. Paste this: 'Write a contract clause that fixes the BTC/USD exchange rate at invoice creation, bars client disputes if market price moves after delivery, and specifies settlement in USD equivalent.' Without it, a Bitcoin payment worth $10,000 on invoice day can arrive worth $7,200 three days later. You eat the difference.

slides.headline: 4) FIND WHICH OF YOUR COSTS YOU CAN PAY IN CRYPTO
slides.body: Your income is now legally protected, cut what you spend next. Paste this: 'Which of these vendor categories accept crypto payments: [list your software subscriptions, ad platforms, freelance contractors]? List by coin accepted and flag any that offer a discount for crypto.' Spending crypto directly skips the taxable conversion step entirely.

slides.headline: 5) WRITE THE EMAIL THAT MOVES CLIENTS TO CRYPTO
slides.body: Paste prompt 5: 'Write a professional client email offering a 2% discount for Bitcoin payment, under 150 words, friendly tone, one sentence on how easy the payment process is.' Businesses offering this skip card processing fees, eliminate chargeback risk, and often collect faster. Paste prompt 6: 'Build a spreadsheet formula that logs each crypto payment by date, coin, USD value at receipt, and running quarterly tax total.' Claude writes the full tracker in one pass.
